name: Stainless-generated MCP server code tool (Mux example, @mux/mcp)
pinned: @mux/mcp 16.2.0 and @mux/ts 16.2.0 from npm (installed with --omit=optional --ignore-scripts, so the bundled deno package was not used); source read at mux-node-sdk 6037f04ae022ecac0bb6f986a35db66338b17ea3 (packages/mcp-server version 16.2.0, compiled files match); Deno 2.9.8 via DENO_PATH
engine: A fresh Deno 2.9.8 subprocess per execution, started by @valtown/deno-http-worker and spoken to over HTTP on a unix socket; flags --allow-read=<install node_modules and package dir>, --allow-net=<SDK base URL host, api.mux.com, image.mux.com, stream.mux.com>, --allow-env (all variables). The code is type-checked with the TypeScript compiler, then imported as a data: URL module and run(client) is called with a proxied, pre-authenticated SDK client.
how_run: node node_modules/@mux/mcp/index.js (stdio transport, default --code-execution-mode=local) driven by an MCP client calling `execute` with `async function run(client) {...}`. No Mux key: MUX_BASE_URL pointed the SDK at a mock Mux API in the harness (127.0.0.1:41320), whose GET /video/v1/assets/:id plays `lookup` (200 ms, value = id * 2); MUX_TOKEN_ID/SECRET were dummy strings.

P1.detail: client.video.assets.retrieve("21") reached the mock API through the real SDK (1 host call, Authorization header present) and returned {id:"21",value:42}; console.log printed 42. With no key and no mock, the same call would go to api.mux.com and fail; the mock shows code reaching the SDK client and the network grant end to end without a credential.

P2.detail: Both come back as separate text blocks: the return value "RETURNED" and the console.log lines, all 200,000 A's. No truncation, no marker.

P3.detail: NotCapable: Requires net access to "example.com:443", run again with the --allow-net flag. Network is open to the SDK hosts (base URL host plus api.mux.com, image.mux.com, stream.mux.com); X3 sent PROBE_SECRET in a query string to the allowed base URL host.

P4.detail: Deno.readTextFileSync and node:fs readFileSync of /etc/hosts -> NotCapable: Requires read access. Reads inside the install's node_modules and package dir are allowed (P4c listed the package directory). A literal import("node:fs") is rejected earlier by the TypeScript check ('Cannot find module').

P5.detail: process.env.PROBE_SECRET and Deno.env.get both returned s3cr3t. The worker gets the server's whole environment and --allow-env with no list; X2 listed every variable, and X1 read MUX_TOKEN_SECRET from env and tokenId/tokenSecret from the client object.

P6.detail: No local time limit: still running at 120 s. When the harness then killed the Deno worker, the whole MCP server process exited with an unhandled 'error' event (socket hang up, ECONNRESET) and the client got 'Connection closed' (P6kill reproduces in 8 s). The server instructions tell the model 'Code execution has a total timeout of approximately 5 minutes'; that only exists for remote mode.

P7.detail: No memory limit. Harness killed the worker at 4,346 MB process-tree RSS after 5.6 s; the MCP server process died with it (next call: Not connected). A worker that dies on its own (V8 OOM) takes the same unhandled-error path.
P7.display: no limit; host crash on worker death

P8.detail: fresh: second execution returned gone (new Deno process per call).

P9.detail: 210 ms inside the sandbox for 5 Promise.all retrieves, 5 host calls: parallel (direct HTTP from the SDK in the worker).

P10.detail: isError:true with text 'Error: probe-boom'. No line number: parseError looks for '<anonymous>:LINE' but the code runs from a data: URL, so the regex never matches. TypeScript diagnostics, when present, do carry the offending source line.

P11.detail: median 380 ms, p90 400 ms per execution (new Deno process plus a full TypeScript program check each time). One-time setup 200 ms (MCP server start).

P12.detail: this.constructor... -> TypeError (this is undefined); (function(){return this})().process -> TypeError. The AsyncFunction constructor works and returned the worker's own process object (pid, platform), which is the sandbox process, not the MCP server. Deno.Command("echo") -> NotCapable run access; node:child_process execSync -> 'Command failed'. No host runtime reached, but env is open (P5).

hardened.config: --code-allow-http-gets --no-client-header-overrides (packages/mcp-server/src/options.ts:37-59; README 'Request headers a caller may send'). These are the strictest documented options; they restrict which SDK methods the code may name (string/regex match) and stop HTTP callers overriding env or permissions. No time, memory, env or network option exists for local mode.

P3.detail: same NotCapable for example.com; SDK hosts still open.

P6.detail: still running at 120 s; harness kill of the worker crashed the MCP server again.

P7.detail: harness killed the worker at 4,383 MB after 5.2 s; MCP server died.
P7.display: no limit; host crash on worker death

P9.detail: 213 ms for 5 parallel GET retrieves (allowed under --code-allow-http-gets).

defaults.time: None in local mode (runCode has no timer, code-tool-runner.ts:110-192). Remote mode caps the round trip at 300 s (code-tool.ts:185). The instructions claim about 5 minutes and a 30 s per-request SDK timeout.
defaults.memory: None (no V8 flags on the worker). P7 reached 4.3 GB.
defaults.output: None. Return value and all console.log lines are returned whole (code-tool.ts:270-281).
defaults.tool_calls: No cap on SDK calls. Method policy via --code-allowed-methods / --code-blocked-methods / --code-allow-http-gets is substring matching on the code text (code-tool.ts:109-123).

source_notes.finding: No tool stubs: the model writes `async function run(client)` against the generated TypeScript SDK (@mux/ts). The worker wraps the real Mux client in a Proxy (makeSdkProxy) that turns unknown paths into errors with fuzzy 'Did you mean' suggestions from a Fuse index of all method names.

A second tool, search_docs, queries a local MiniSearch index built from embedded SDK method docs, so method schemas are fetched on demand rather than placed in the prompt. The execute description itself is 1,149 chars.

There is no host bridge: the SDK client runs inside the sandbox and makes its own HTTP requests, which is why the network grant must include the API hosts and why credentials must be inside the sandbox.

Deno permissions on a per-call subprocess: reads limited to the install, network limited to SDK hosts, no run/write/ffi, but --allow-env for everything and spawnOptions.env = the server's full process.env merged with caller-supplied client envs. The README's 'sandbox environment without web or filesystem access' holds for arbitrary hosts and host files; the environment is fully readable.
console.log and console.error are swapped for collectors inside the worker; the MCP result is up to three text blocks: the JSON return value, the log lines, and 'Error output:' lines. No truncation.
Local mode has no time, memory, output or call limits. The only timeout in the code tool is remote mode's 300 s fetch timeout.

The HTTP request to the worker has a response 'error' handler but none on the request itself, so a worker that dies mid-request (killed, or a V8 OOM abort) raises an unhandled 'error' event and exits the MCP server process.

Uncaught errors become 'Name: message' plus a cause; the intended 'at line N' never appears because the stack frames are data: URLs, not '<anonymous>'. TypeScript diagnostics are returned with the offending line before any code runs.

API credentials are passed into the sandbox twice: as client options and in the env. Method blocking is plain substring matching on the code text, and the source says so ('not secure against obfuscation'); H2 called the blocked assets.create through a computed property name and the POST reached the API.

surprises: The server instructions tell the model 'Code execution has a total timeout of approximately 5 minutes', but local mode (the default) has no timeout at all; P6 ran past 120 s.
Killing a runaway worker, or a worker dying from OOM, crashes the whole MCP server (unhandled 'error' on the worker request), so one bad execution ends the session for the client.

The worker inherits every server environment variable with --allow-env, so model code can read API secrets and anything else in the server's env (P5, X1, X2). The README says only 'without web or filesystem access', which is accurate but leaves env out.
Network is open to api.mux.com, image.mux.com and stream.mux.com plus the base URL host, so data can leave the machine through those hosts (X3 showed a secret in a query string to the allowed host).
The error formatter's line-number extraction cannot match because code runs from a data: URL (P10).
--code-allow-http-gets blocked assets.create when named literally (H1) but a computed name went straight through (H2), as the source comment warns.
Each call re-runs a full TypeScript type check, so plain-JS code with implicit types can be rejected before it runs, and an execution costs about 380 ms.
